title: Grade 12 Mathematics — Differential Equations
description: Differential Equations — order, degree, solutions, separable, homogeneous, linear (CBSE Ch. 9)
subject: mathematics

questions.question: The order of the differential equation d²y/dx² + dy/dx + y = 0 is:
questions.explanation: The order of a differential equation is the order of the highest derivative present. Here the highest derivative is d²y/dx² (second derivative), so the order is 2.

questions.question: The degree of the differential equation (d²y/dx²)³ + dy/dx = x² is:
questions.explanation: The degree is the power (exponent) of the highest-order derivative, once the equation is written as a polynomial in derivatives. Here, the highest derivative d²y/dx² appears to the power 3, so the degree is 3.

questions.question: Which of the following is a solution of dy/dx = y?
questions.explanation: For y = eˣ: dy/dx = eˣ = y. ✓ This is the equation describing exponential growth, whose solution is y = Ceˣ where C is an arbitrary constant.

questions.question: The number of arbitrary constants in the general solution of a differential equation of order n is:
questions.explanation: The general solution of an nth-order ODE contains exactly n arbitrary constants. Each integration step introduces one constant.

questions.question: Solve: dy/dx = x². The general solution is:
questions.explanation: Separating and integrating: dy = x² dx → y = ∫x² dx = x³/3 + C.

questions.question: Solve: dy/dx = (1 + y²)/(1 + x²). This equation is of the type:
questions.explanation: Rewriting: dy/(1+y²) = dx/(1+x²). Variables can be separated on both sides → variable separable type. Integrating gives tan⁻¹y = tan⁻¹x + C.

questions.question: A differential equation dy/dx = f(x, y) is homogeneous if:
options: f(tx, ty) = t^n · f(x, y) for some n
questions.explanation: A function f(x,y) is homogeneous of degree n if f(tx, ty) = tⁿ f(x,y). A homogeneous DE has f homogeneous of degree 0, i.e., f(tx,ty) = f(x,y). It can be solved by substituting y = vx.

questions.question: The integrating factor (IF) for the linear equation dy/dx + Py = Q (where P, Q are functions of x) is:
questions.explanation: For the standard linear ODE dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x), the integrating factor is μ = e^(∫P dx). Multiplying through by μ reduces the left side to d(μy)/dx.

questions.question: The integrating factor for dy/dx + y/x = x² is:
questions.explanation: P = 1/x. IF = e^(∫(1/x) dx) = e^(ln x) = x.

questions.question: The general solution of dy/dx = −y/x is:
questions.explanation: Separating: dy/y = −dx/x → ln|y| = −ln|x| + ln|C| → ln|xy| = ln|C| → xy = C.

questions.question: What is the order of the DE obtained by eliminating a and b from y = ax² + bx?
questions.explanation: There are 2 arbitrary constants (a and b). Eliminating 2 constants requires 2 differentiations, giving a 2nd-order DE.

questions.question: Solve the initial value problem: dy/dx = 2x, y(0) = 3. The particular solution is:
questions.explanation: Integrating: y = x² + C. Applying y(0) = 3: 3 = 0 + C → C = 3. Particular solution: y = x² + 3.

questions.question: The degree of the differential equation d²y/dx² + sin(dy/dx) = 0 is:
questions.explanation: The degree is defined only when the DE can be written as a polynomial in its derivatives. Since sin(dy/dx) is a transcendental function of the derivative, the degree is NOT defined.

questions.question: The solution of dy/dx + y tan x = sec x is:
options: y cos x = sin x + C
y sec x = tan x + C
y = sin x + C cos x
y sin x = cos x + C
questions.explanation: This is linear: P = tan x, IF = e^∫tan x dx = e^(ln|sec x|) = sec x. Multiplying: d(y·sec x)/dx = sec²x → y sec x = tan x + C → y cos x = sin x + C·cos x. Simplifying gives y cos x = sin x + C (with the C absorbed).

questions.question: A population P grows at a rate proportional to its size. This is modelled by:
questions.explanation: Exponential growth/decay: 'rate proportional to size' means dP/dt = kP. The solution is P = P₀·eᵏᵗ (growth if k > 0, decay if k < 0).
